class.name: JarBodyLight
class.brief_description: Makes its JarCelestialBody a star that lights the scene.
class.description: Put it under a [JarCelestialBody] (the sun). Every frame it aims a [DirectionalLight3D] ([member JarBodyLayer.sun], else the first one in the scene) from the body's center at the camera, so the light comes from wherever the star is: as the universe turns around the anchor (a spinning planet, its orbit around the sun) the sun rises and sets. With [member physical_size] it also gives the light the star's real angular size, which sets the sun disk a sky shader draws from [code]LIGHT0_SIZE[/code] and the softness of shadows. Color, energy and shadows stay on the light. Inside a [JarBodyAtmosphere] the light reaches the camera through the air: it reddens as the star sets and is gone below the horizon (balanced so the star overhead keeps the light's own color). [b]Moons:[/b] with [member reflects] set to the star's JarBodyLight, it makes its body a moon instead: its own light ([member JarBodyLayer.sun] must be set, to a second [DirectionalLight3D]) shines from the moon at the camera, [member energy] strong at full moon and following the phase (a Lambertian sphere: [method get_phase_at]), reddened through the air like the sun, and draws no disk in the sky (the moon itself is drawn). It lights the night side, and the clouds at night. The light joins the group [code]"jar_body_light"[/code] ([JarVoxelUniverse] leaves it to this node and does not turn it with the sky), and [code]"jar_star_light"[/code] or [code]"jar_moon_light"[/code]: the other layers ([JarBodyWater], [JarBodyAtmosphere], [JarBodyClouds]) use the star's as their sun and the moon's as [code]moon_direction[/code] and [code]moon_color[/code]. The star itself is not drawn (it is usually far beyond the camera's far plane): the sky shows its disk. [method get_direction_at] and [method get_angular_diameter_at] give what effects such as a lens flare or an atmosphere need.

method.name: get_angular_diameter_at
method.description: The star's apparent diameter seen from [param global_position], in degrees (from its effective radius and distance).

method.name: get_phase_at
method.description: Of a moon: the part of full moon light it sends to [param global_position], from where the star it [member reflects] is: 1 at full moon, 0 at new moon.

method.name: get_direction_at
method.description: Unit direction from [param global_position] towards the star's center.

members.member: Of a moon: its light's energy at full moon.
Sets the light's angular size ([member Light3D.light_angular_distance]) to the star's apparent size at the camera. Off: the light's own setting is kept.
The star whose light this body reflects: set it to make this a moon (see the description). Empty: a star.
